Bring the locations of a store into step

Source: R/sync.R
store_sync.Rd

Copies datasets from one location, the source (by default the primary), to the other locations of the connection: every dataset whose copy in a target differs from the source's (another version, or another entry) or, where the scope below allows it, is missing. Only the files a target lacks are sent, each verified by MD5; the catalogs of a target are switched last, so that its readers always see a complete version. A geospatial dataset's index table travels with it.

Usage

store_sync(
  st,
  datasets = NULL,
  all = FALSE,
  to = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  delete = FALSE,
  force = FALSE,
  dry_run = FALSE
)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect(). It is updated in place.

datasets

NULL for every dataset of the source, or names of datasets (full names, or last parts that are unique in the source). With delete = TRUE it restricts the deletions too, and a full name the source does not hold is accepted.

all

TRUE copies every dataset of the source to every target, including datasets a secondary does not hold, but not the datasets kept in the primary only (see "Scope"). FALSE (the default) refreshes in a secondary only the datasets it already holds (see "Scope"). Cannot be combined with datasets.

to

NULL for every location other than the source, or the addresses of some of them.

from

NULL for the primary, or the address of the location to copy from.

delete

TRUE deletes from each target the datasets the source does not hold.

force

TRUE copies over versions that are newer in a target, and lets delete = TRUE delete datasets from the primary.

dry_run

TRUE reports what would be copied, deleted and found in conflict, and changes nothing.

Value

A tibble, invisibly, one row per target location: location, status ("synced", "same" when nothing was copied or deleted, "conflict" when the target holds a newer version of a dataset, "behind" when it failed, "unavailable", or "to sync" with dry_run = TRUE), the list columns datasets (copied, or to copy), deleted (deleted, or to delete), kept (not deleted from the primary without force) and conflicts; then the datasets left out by the scope (those kept in the primary only included): skipped (a list column of names), skipped_files and skipped_bytes (the files of those datasets the target lacks, and their size: at most what all = TRUE would send); then files (files sent, or to send), bytes and seconds. A status of "same" can go with skipped datasets.

Details

With from set to a secondary location, work done there (for example through a connection whose primary was that location, while the primary could not be reached) is brought to the primary and to the other secondaries.

Scope

By default (datasets = NULL, all = FALSE) a secondary location receives only the datasets it already holds, at any version: they are brought to the source's version, and nothing new is copied there. The call says which datasets were not copied to each secondary, with the number of files and the bytes a full sync would send at most (an empty secondary is named as such). all = TRUE copies every dataset of the source, except the datasets kept in the primary only (store_write(locations = "primary")) to a secondary that does not hold them; they are listed apart among the datasets not copied. datasets = copies the named datasets, whether or not a secondary holds them, those kept in the primary only included (the copy keeps that setting). A secondary that holds a primary-only dataset gets it refreshed like any other dataset it holds. The primary, as a target (from a secondary), always receives every dataset of the source.

Conflicts

When a target holds another version of a dataset and its entry was updated later than the source's (the times recorded in the catalogs), the dataset is not copied there: it is a conflict. Every other copy and deletion goes ahead; after the last target the call aborts with class rcs_error_sync_conflict, listing the conflicts, and the condition's field result holds the result tibble. force = TRUE copies the source over the newer version instead. Every version of a target that is replaced by another one is listed in one warning (class rcs_warning_sync_overwrite). The times compared are those of the machines that wrote; their clocks may differ.

Deletions

By default store_sync() never deletes a dataset: datasets found only in a target are left alone (see store_status(), status "extra"). With delete = TRUE they are deleted from that target, with their index table, after its copies, as store_delete() does for one location (the history kept). The primary is a target only when from is a secondary; datasets are deleted there only with force = TRUE, and are otherwise reported in the result column kept. Files of a version a target replaces are deleted when the dataset keeps no history, as in store_write().

A target that fails is reported as behind with a warning, and the next one is synced; running the call again sends only what is still missing.

See also

store_status() to compare the locations, store_copy() for one dataset between any two locations; vignette("locations") for syncs from a secondary, conflicts and deletions.

Examples

root <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-sync")
store_create(file.path(root, "copy"))
#> ✔ Created an empty store in
#>   /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy.
st <- store_connect(file.path(root, "primary"), create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(100, seed = 1), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 100 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/primary  2/2
#>   files sent  23.8 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.

# A connection with a secondary location that missed the write
st <- store_connect(file.path(root, "primary"),
  secondary = file.path(root, "copy")
)
#> ℹ Secondary /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy is
#>   empty.
#>   Use `store_sync(st, all = TRUE)` to copy every dataset, or `store_sync(st,
#>   datasets = )` to copy some.
store_status(st)
#> Source: /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/primary
#> Locations: [1] /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   dataset     location status  newer primary_version  location_version
#>   <chr>       <chr>    <chr>   <chr> <chr>            <chr>           
#> 1 sales/daily [1]      missing NA    0f9e01793cbea58a NA              
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: primary_updated <dttm>, location_updated <dttm>

# The secondary is empty: a default sync copies nothing and says so
store_sync(st)
#> ℹ Syncing the datasets already held by each secondary location, from the
#>   primary /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/primary
#>   to 1 secondary location.
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy     nothing
#>   copied
#> ℹ Synced only the datasets already in each secondary location.
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy is empty: 1
#>   dataset not copied (2 files, 23.8 kB).
#>   Use `store_sync(st, all = TRUE)` to copy every dataset, or `datasets = ` to
#>   copy some.

# Every dataset
store_sync(st, all = TRUE, dry_run = TRUE)
#> ℹ Dry run: nothing is changed.
#> ℹ Syncing 1 dataset from the primary
#>   /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/primary to 1
#>   secondary location.
#> • secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy     would
#>   copy 1 dataset, 2 files (23.8 kB): "sales/daily"
store_sync(st, all = TRUE)
#> ℹ Syncing 1 dataset from the primary
#>   /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/primary to 1
#>   secondary location.
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy     1
#>   dataset, 2/2 files sent  23.8 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files sent to 1 location. Catalogs updated.

# Work done on the secondary alone, brought back to the primary
offline <- store_connect(file.path(root, "copy"))
store_write(offline, rcs_sim_table(50, seed = 2), "sales/weekly",
  title = "Weekly sales", description = "Simulated weekly sales."
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/weekly": 50 rows in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy  1/1
#>   files sent  11.7 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
store_sync(st, from = file.path(root, "copy"))
#> ℹ Syncing 2 datasets from the secondary
#>   /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy to 1
#>   location.
#> ✔ primary    /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/primary  1
#>   dataset, 1/1 files sent  11.7 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file sent to 1 location. Catalogs updated.
store_status(st)
#> Source: /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/primary
#> Locations: [1] /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-sync/copy
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   dataset      location status newer primary_version  location_version
#>   <chr>        <chr>    <chr>  <chr> <chr>            <chr>           
#> 1 sales/daily  [1]      same   NA    0f9e01793cbea58a 0f9e01793cbea58a
#> 2 sales/weekly [1]      same   NA    e8bcbde15b3cbebc e8bcbde15b3cbebc
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: primary_updated <dttm>, location_updated <dttm>
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
